goal: Quantify every rev B deviation against the client form and playbook at the stated monthly fee and file the annex under the commissioned filename.
prompt:
You are supporting outside counsel on the Northgale Systems engagement adverse to Corvid Analytics. First query the matter file to locate, and then read in full, each of: (1) the Northgale client-form master services agreement (the v2 execution-ready base, which states the monthly base fee); (2) the operative Corvid counter-draft markup (the current revision from Corvid's counsel — ignore withdrawn earlier-round transmittals kept in the file for history); (3) the Northgale commercial contracting playbook, 2026 edition; and (4) the general counsel's engagement instruction letter of 14 July 2026 (which directs how exposure must be quantified). Then draft a numbered deviation-and-exposure annex for the negotiation file that, for EACH rev B change, states the client-form position, the markup position, the playbook standard and fallback, and the dollar impact computed from figures stated in the documents — including at minimum: the liability-cap value at the client-form measurement period, at the markup's proposed measurement period, and at the playbook fallback floor, each computed at the stated monthly base fee; the maximum monthly service credit under the client-form credit cap versus the markup's reduced cap; and the cost of the proposed full-fee wind-down period versus the playbook's out-of-pocket-only position. Create the deliverable with documents_create using title exactly corvid-msa-deviation-and-exposure-annex.docx and doc_type exactly deliverable. Compute only from figures that appear in the documents; do not invent amounts.

reference_args.body:
DEVIATION AND EXPOSURE ANNEX — CORVID REV B VS NORTHGALE CLIENT FORM v2 AND 2026 PLAYBOOK
All dollar figures computed at the client-form base fee of $85,000 per month (Section 4.1).

1. Liability cap (Section 9.1). Client form: 24-month measurement period = $2,040,000. Rev B: 12-month period = $1,020,000. Playbook fallback floor: 18 months = $1,530,000. Impact: the rev B ask reduces recoverable exposure by $1,020,000 against the client form and is $510,000 below the approved fallback floor. Out of policy — CLO approval required.
2. Carve-outs (Section 9.2). Rev B deletes the gross negligence / willful misconduct carve-out, converting an uncapped exposure into a capped one at the Section 9.1 level. Non-negotiable per playbook; joint CLO/CFO approval required for any deletion.
3. Renewal (Section 2.2). One (1) year periods become two (2) years, doubling the committed renewal tail at $1,020,000 of fees per renewal year of lock-in. No approved fallback exists — CLO approval required.
4. Termination for convenience (Section 7.2). 30 days becomes 90 days: up to 60 additional days of fees, approximately $170,000, beyond the client form; playbook fallback permits at most 45 days (approximately $42,500 beyond standard).
5. Wind-down (new Section 7.4). 60 days at the full base fee is approximately $170,000 of committed spend; playbook position is a 30-day cap with compensation limited to documented out-of-pocket costs and non-cancelable third-party commitments.
6. Service credits (Section 11.2). Maximum monthly credit falls from 20% of the base fee ($17,000) to 10% ($8,500); playbook fallback floor is 15% ($12,750).
7. Late interest (Section 4.3). 1.0% becomes 1.5% per month — $850 versus $1,275 per month per $85,000 outstanding; playbook maximum is 1.0%.
8. Suspension (new Section 4.4). Suspension after 15 days past due, with no cure notice; playbook requires a 30-day cure notice and CFO sign-off for any suspension right.

Prepared for the negotiation file per the general counsel's instruction letter of 14 July 2026.
